newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T. Industries reports 5 pct increase in profits.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T. Industries reports 5 pct increase in profits.

text.p: B.A.T Industries Plc reported a five percent increase in its 1996 profits to 2.495 billion on Wednesday and dismissed any liability for damages claimed by smokers in the United States.

"We continue to believe that B.A.T Industries itself has no potential liability in any U.S. tobacco litigation," said chairman Lord Cairns in a statement. Despite hopes amongst investors the tobacco industry "remains confident of its ability, ultimately, to win cases and has no intention of proposing a settlement," he said.
However, Cairns said the company would be prepared to "evaluate proposals from third parties to provide relief from all current and future suits, provided that they were in shareholders' interests".
The company's profits included an exceptionally high charge of 160 million pounds ($258.1 million) for the year for 30 year old environmental claims against its Eagle Star insurance unit.

B.A.T's tobacco business turned in a 7 percent overall improvement in local currency to 1.634 billion pounds with group volumes four percent ahead and world market share increasing to 12.8 percent from 12.4 percent.

Trading profit from financial services grew by an underlying eight percent to 1.2 billion with strong performances from Farmers and Allied Dunbar. The company recommended an eight percent increase in the base dividend to 26.0p.

Lord Cairns said B.A.T plans to improve long term growth prospects and increase shareholder return. "We continue to evaluate business oppurtunities and issues of corporate structure that will enable us to meet them," he said.
